newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia -- a killing every 20 minutes.
newsitem.headline: Colombia -- a killing every 20 minutes.

text.p: Political bloodshed, common crime and homicide claimed the lives of 26,710 Colombians in 1996, a 5.4 percent increase over 1995, when the country saw 25,330 killings, a National Police report said on Tuesday.
The figure for 1996, which excludes 6,158 people killed in car accidents, works out to three violent deaths every hour or a killing every 20 minutes.

Medellin, the northwestern city of about 2 million people often described as the murder capital of the world, maintained its grim reputation in 1996 with 5,323 murders -- an average of 14.5 per day -- the police report said. The second most violent city was the capital, Bogota, with 3,291 murders.

"Violentologists," academics who specialise in studying Colombia's runaway murder rate, say it has its roots in the period known as "La Violencia" between 1948 and 1957 when as many as 300,000 people were killed in a virtual civil war between members of the Conservative and Liberal parties.
The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's largest and oldest leftist guerrilla group, grew out of Liberal Party peasant militias formed in 1948.

Along with violence stemming from the drug trade, experts say a leading factor fuelling the high murder rate is Colombia's weak judicial system and the fact that more than 90 percent of all crimes in the country go unpunished.
